# Outbound experiment: two weeks of peers publishing through the FM gate

## Context

Graduated from [D#19500](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/discussions/19500) (*Outbound as a measured experiment: peers publish in public through a gate, and read what comes back*) at its §6.2 quorum of 2026-10-10 22:21Z. The operator's hypothesis (2026-10-09): the team has been inbound — frontier work on an equal-peer institution and Qt-class dock layouts that almost nobody notices — and the way to test it is a repeatable outbound cadence with a scoreboard, before anyone reads silence as a verdict. This ticket is the **experiment itself**: two weeks, measured, then a verdict. It sits beside #14790 (the 13.2 launch playbook, which already defines the release sequence that "produces measured strangers"). The product capability the experiment runs on — the FM gate — is filed separately (Brain · Institution · Brain, one ADR); this ticket consumes it and does not build it.

## The Problem

Week zero, measured 2026-10-10 (GitHub traffic API, fourteen-day window, the top-ten referrer list): `neomjs/neo` 4,470 views / 746 uniques (104–154 a day, median 127); referrers `github.com` 69 uniques, Google 75, `linkedin.com` 8, aocr.org 6, neomjs.com 4, reddit 3, medium 1, Bing 2, Brave 2, DuckDuckGo 1 — `t.co` absent from the returned ten (if ranked by count, GitHub-attributed X referrals are bounded by one visit; a conditional bound on one instrument, never a count). `/issues` drew 101 uniques and the repository root 111: strangers read our issues. `neomjs/neo-agent-institution`: 19 uniques, essentially the team. The Fleet Manager repository has no forks and no outside star; the last Medium post is a year old against an audience of 800+. That is the floor the experiment must clear, per channel and per format.

## The Architectural Reality

- **Channels and accounts (D#19500 OQ-1, the operator's decisions):** X — one account per peer, labeled automated, created and authorized once by the operator against the team's developer app, posting as itself through the FM gate; LinkedIn — the `neomjs` organisation page posting as *Neo.mjs* with the author's signature line, through the Community Management API under the operator's page-admin authorization (by his hand until that approval lands; a member profile per peer is barred by LinkedIn's agreement §2.1 / §8.2); Medium — the existing account, team-written articles with inline section authors, the operator presses publish.
- **The gate (OQ-2, the operator's design):** a peer never publishes; it sends the operator one typed A2A request (the mailbox's returned `MESSAGE:` id is the key; the payload an immutable revision with a content digest); the operator's Fleet Manager holds one switch per peer × channel — `approve each` · `approve the batch` · `auto-approve after a cross-family review attestation` · `auto-approve` — read at publish time, operator-authenticated and audited; the Fleet-side executor publishes the approved revision under the account's own credential, at most once, and records the provider id. Week one: X posts at `approve the batch`; replies by the operator's hand or waiting until X's automation classification is settled; LinkedIn by his hand; Medium human.
- **The format and the cold start (OQ-7):** links are taxed in X's price ($0.20 a post with a URL against $0.015) and in both platforms' reach, so the receipt rides in the post (a clip, a capture, a number with its context) and the link in the first own reply; new accounts have no graph, so week one distributes hypothesis (a) through **replies to the questions the harness makers put to their users** — Codex's lead (`@thsottiaux`) to the GPT peers; Boris Cherny, Lydia Hallie and Andrej Karpathy's posts to the Claude peers — never a question outside our practice, never under an announcement; hypothesis (b) through media-first posts (the 13.2 film's clips, #15252). The operator's own account as amplifier is his voice and his call.
- **The scoreboard (OQ-4):** per object (post · link-reply · reply) `public_metrics` and, for owned objects within 30 days, `non_public_metrics` (`url_link_clicks`, `user_profile_clicks`, `engagements`); per account per day new followers (Owned Reads, $0.001); per week GitHub referrers against the week-zero line — a censored top ten, an absent domain `unknown` and bounded, never zero; every metric with source, window, claim class and confound bound (Brain #123's rule); repository visitors and stars stay correlated observations. The gate measures itself: minutes per approval or batch, edits and drops per request, per peer and channel. The private half (goals, targets) lives in the business repository's workflow; this ticket carries the public-safe aggregates.
- **The policy text (OQ-3):** the `blog-post` skill widens to social posts with one load-on-demand reference (boundaries, the request form with revisions and formats, the review attestation) — a skills-repo leaf, filed with the gate.
- **The URL precondition:** a post is shareable today (the portal's hash route and GitHub) but unfurls with the site-wide card; the static routes exist on `dev` (#19503) and go live with a manual publish of `neomjs/pages` — this ticket names who runs it and when (AC-3).

## The Fix — the run

1. **Week zero is recorded first**, with matching windows: the engine repository's fourteen-day views, uniques and top-ten referrers (above); the June/July portal posts' and the Medium account's numbers for a first-N-days window where the source can still give one, `unknown` where it cannot; a lifetime total never stands in for a week-one baseline.
2. **The clock starts at the first new post.** Prerequisites the operator holds: the X developer app on pay-per-use credits (the $20 card credit covers week one at the planned cadence) and each peer account's one-time authorization; the LinkedIn Community Management application for the `neomjs` page (the long pole — LinkedIn runs by his hand until it lands). Prerequisite the team holds: the FM gate's first slice, or, until it ships, the operator's hand on the publish from the requests the peers file.
3. **Week one:** hypothesis (a) through answers under the harness makers' questions, (b) through media-first posts, (d) as the packaging story; (c) parked until an outside first-run receipt exists. Every request names its hypothesis and format; per-peer voices carry different work and receipts.
4. **Daily:** replies read; answers drafted as requests. **Weekly:** the public-safe aggregates posted here per channel, format and hypothesis against week zero; the gate's minutes, edits and drops; the pages publish's state.
5. **End of week one:** the edit-rate falsifier is read first — if most requests went out edited, the bottleneck is draft quality, not the gate.
6. **End of week two:** the verdict, qualitative — which format and hypothesis drew replies and clicks, not views; whether a reply under someone else's post moved more readers to a receipt than a post of our own; whether any conversation reached a trial or a pilot question; what to stop. The reading loop (OQ-6) is decided then, and only for a channel that answered.

**Early stop:** a boundary breach in public (the correction is posted, the channel's switch returns to `approve each`) or the edit-rate falsifier.

**Decision Record:** `REQUIRED` for the FM gate, carried by its Brain leaf (the request contract, the custody rule, the switch) — not by this ticket. **Decision Record impact** of this ticket: none.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1 — Every X peer account carries X's automated-account label and was authorized by the operator; no LinkedIn member profile exists for a peer; no seat holds a social credential. Recorded here before the first post.
- [ ] AC-2 — Every post of the experiment traces to a mailbox-identified request, the approved revision's digest, the approval (or the switch state that auto-released it, read at publish time) and a provider id; no post was published by a seat; posts published by the operator's hand before the gate ships are recorded with the same fields by hand.
- [ ] AC-3 — The pages publish of the blog routes has a named owner and a date here; until it lands, no post links a portal hash route as its receipt.
- [ ] AC-4 — Week zero is recorded here before the first new post, with source and window per number; the gate's own numbers (minutes per approval or batch, edits and drops per request) are recorded from the first batch.
- [ ] AC-5 — Every weekly aggregate carries source, observation window, claim class and confound bound; an absent referrer is `unknown` and bounded, never zero; no post → star attribution is claimed without a per-object click.
- [ ] AC-6 — Every request names its hypothesis and format (post · link-reply · reply); week one carries only (a), (b) and (d); no reply goes to a question outside our practice or under an announcement; the boundaries of D#19500 §4 hold on every post, checked by a reviewer of another family under the `blog-post` reference.
- [ ] AC-7 — Week one's reading separates the three formats and reads the edit-rate falsifier first; the result is posted here.
- [ ] AC-8 — The verdict is posted here at the end of week two: which format and hypothesis drew replies and clicks, whether any conversation reached a trial or a pilot question, what to stop.
- [ ] AC-9 — The reading loop (OQ-6) is decided at the verdict, for a channel that answered; the decision links its Brain leaf under ADR 0036 or records that none is filed.

## Out of Scope

Building the FM gate (its ADR and three leaves are filed with their own ACs); the `blog-post` widening (its skills leaf); the reading provider (after the verdict); the article stock's own tickets (#9849, #9850, #19058, #9852); the operator's entitlements as work items — they are his prerequisites, recorded here when met; any post before week zero is recorded.

## Avoided Traps

- **A link in the post** — taxed in price and reach; the receipt rides in the post, the link in the first own reply.
- **Hashtags as the lever** — zero to two, a recorded variable.
- **Post → star attribution** — repository visitors and stars are correlated observations; the per-object click and the referrer are the trail.
- **A reply under an announcement** — an answer needs a question; while the open-source applications are pending, such a reply reads as a pitch.
- **A lifetime total as week zero** — matching windows or `unknown`.
- **Coordinated amplification among our own accounts** — no like, repost or reply rings; peer-to-peer exchanges only on genuine disagreement or review, disclosed.
- **Treating `approve each` as a platform exemption** — it is our release control; X's classification of an operator-approved API reply is unresolved, and the executor's reply verb stays disabled until it is settled.
